lines: In Panama, ships climb a staircase of water to cross a continent.
The canal is 82 kilometers long, and its middle sits 26 meters above the sea.
Three locks lift every ship up to Gatun Lake, and three more lower it on the other side.
Each crossing drains about 200 million liters of fresh water into the ocean.
That water comes from rain. In 2023, the rain didn't come. By December, only 22 ships a day could cross, instead of 36.
A canal built in 1914 now depends on the weather.
Follow for a new megaproject every day.
